item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
The way the entry is written, I'm left with the initial impression that SCP-356 is a corpse that causes phone lines to talk about him. Then, it mentions that he died after the interview… and I [i]think[/i] the phenomena ended with him except for the one phone call in 2009 implying that the voice is now relating his ascent into the celestial planes?

I feel like this could be written to either indicate the report at the time of his life with an addendum at the end indicating his death and the follow-up events or written to straightforwardly indicate that the SCP is the corpse and that in the past, it showed this ability / curse / whatever.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I like this quite a lot.

Nitpick: The voice for 356-A doesn't really fit, and I'm not sure it should even be capable of direct interaction with staff. It feels like it'd work better as an affectless, droning recital of 356's life, more like an audiotape of Ben Stein reading excerpts from an encyclopedia than somebody's snarky dickhead id. Something that can be guided by screaming the same question enough times in this poor guy's face, but can't acknowledge or openly respond to stimulus independently. That it's a bit of subjectivity fuck inheres in the concept itself; having A give us the director's commentary isn't really necessary.

One more: The second collapsible is a bit dicey. It upsets the flow of the narrative just to trade us one relevant piece of information, namely that the U.S. is still running programs like this. That can be shifted to containment procedures or general addenda with no real loss to the piece. As for the blackboxing and Project ███████████, they help add to the feeling of unearthly Cold War paranoia, but they're also a bit clumsy and probably not worth the collapsible tease. And there are people here who can tell you how much I love blackboxing.

All said, this is still very good and easily worth an upvote.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: I object to this being phrased as a "power", as he's not an X-Man. Anyway. It's not supposed to be an asset to him, it's the end result of an unconventional interrogation program that he was ensnared in during his work. Elements of the CIA were working on anomalous stuff in the 1980s, to the point that the Foundation had to put a stop to it. It's replicable, or at least assumed to be so, because SCP-356 is the result of CIA efforts, and he is now incapable of withholding any sort of information whatsoever. Or at least he was before he keeled over.

item.content:encoded:
That's what I came to say, more or less.

It seems to me that this file would have been written while he was an active containee. Maybe the test logs would be past tense, but at least the description should have been in present tense. Unless you're thinking the Foundation went back through and retro-actively edited the verbage after he died, which doesn't really seem reasonable.

Minor technical matter aside, I kind of like it. It doesn't blow me away, but I am intrigued by what happened to cause his oddity. It's obviously somehow tied to his past exploits, but was it an anomalously enhanced interrogation method applied to him, or a side-effect of something he encountered on a mission, or what? Making me want to know more is one of my auto-upvote conditions.

Other than that, I don't see much to this one. I thought the phone calls were going to be creepy, but it's, more like this guy's ghost is trapped in the radio-ether around him and he's transmitting it. It's well written and all (no spelling or grammar mistakes) but it isn't scary, or creepy, or thought provoking and doesn't provoke much of an emotional response.
